conviction_note: Near non-result: the counterparties (Hubbell, Arcosa) confirm strong utility demand, but Valmont says it is limited by supply, not demand. US hot-rolled steel kept rising after the 2026-07-17 assumption behind the guide, against margins the CFO already said were squeezed. The upside-paid skew, 5 of 7 prior prints up and the stock 24% off its high lean slightly up; the Q2 beat-and-raise sold off 3.9%. The findings sum to +0.3, and the scaled number, (2*0.52-1)*7.5, is also +0.3.
bar: Q3 2026 adj EPS $5.73-5.74 on revenue ~$1.11bn (two Benzinga snapshots, agreeing: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VMI/earnings-forecasts , https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/VMI/earnings-forecasts). Company FY26 guide is diluted EPS $22.25-23.50, sales $4.3-4.45bn (8-K ex99.1, 2026-07-21: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000102729/000110465926085223/vmi-20260721xex99d1.htm). Year to date EPS is $11.65, so the guide implies H2 EPS of $10.60-11.85 (midpoint $11.23). MarketBeat's FY consensus of $23.08 implies H2 consensus of about $11.43 (Q3 $5.73 + Q4 about $5.70), which sits above the guide midpoint, so the street already expects the upper half of the guide. Year-ago Q3 was adj EPS $4.98 on $1.05bn.
positioning_check: Short interest 417.6K shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 2.2% of shares outstanding, 1.98 days to cover, down 8.3% from 455.2K on 09-15. Borrow fee 0.3%, 250K shares available (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/vmi/, read 2026-10-19). Not crowded. Baseline: 25-delta skew of -4.6 vol points, so upside is paid. findings.finding: US hot-rolled coil kept rising after the 2026-07-17 steel-futures assumption behind the raised guide. Nucor's CSP was $1,135/st on 2026-07-20, $1,190 on 09-08 and $1,230 in its 10-05 letter, about +8% since the guide was set; Kallanish put HRC at $1,210-1,220/st on 10-02 against $825-865 a year earlier. Valmont is steel-intensive (poles, towers, pivots). On the Q2 call the CFO said material inflation (steel +27-30% YTD, diesel +45%) was compressing Infrastructure incrementals and would continue in Q3, with H2 Infrastructure margins 'consistent with the first half'. Further rises raise the risk of a Q3 margin miss against 17.6% in Q2, or a cautious Q4/2027 margin tone.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (07-21): beat and raise, but the call flagged sequential margin compression from materials, and the stock fell 3.9% (baseline). Q4 2025 (02-17): margin and Ag miss, -6.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: The company's own steel assumption is dated 2026-07-17 and no Valmont update has come since. Had the market priced further margin pressure, Q3/FY consensus would have been cut since August, but MarketBeat still shows FY $23.08, in the upper half of the guide. The Oct 5-14 slide (-7%) may partly reflect this; no source ties it to steel.
findings.independence: July levels: SMU, https://www.steelmarketupdate.com/2026/07/20/nucor-holds-spot-hr-price-at-1135-ton/ (Nucor CSP $1,135/st on 07-20). Nucor's own Q3 guide (higher steel ASPs) is at https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/nucor-issues-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-expects-higher-steel-mills-and-steel-products-earnings-1478837.htm. The company's cost commentary comes from the Q2 call transcript, https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-valmont-industries-inc-stock/. All three are macro proxies: Valmont passes steel through to utility customers with a lag, and part of the rise was in futures on 07-17.

findings.finding: Two counterparties and peers that reported after Valmont's July 21 call confirm utility T&D demand. Hubbell's Q2 (07-28) had net sales +15% (organic +10%), utility T&D demand cited, and a raised FY outlook. Arcosa's Q2 (08-05) had utility and related structures backlog at a record $648.1m, up 49% since the start of the year, revenue +12% on volume and pricing, and segment EBITDA margin up 180bp to 20.4%. This supports NA Utility (+33.9% in Q2), the line behind the Infrastructure guide raise. Arcosa is also converting wind-tower plants to poles, which adds competing capacity.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (04-21): utility-driven beat and EPS raise, +11.9%. Q2 2026: utility +33.9% and Infrastructure guide raised, yet -3.9%. The utility line has paid once and been sold once.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: utility strength is the known bull case, and Valmont says growth is supply-limited. The added information is Arcosa's +49% backlog build, against Valmont's Infrastructure backlog of only +2% in H1 ($1,548m to $1,584m). That points to strong demand into Q3 and some share risk. If the market fully believed in Q3 utility upside, the stock would not sit 24% off its high with FY consensus at the guide's upper half.
findings.independence: Hubbell Q2 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000048898/000162828026049934/exhibit991_07282026.htm . This is a separate document from Arcosa's, so the two sources are independent of each other, but both are peer proxies, not Valmont numbers.

findings.finding: The bar sits above the guide midpoint (H2 consensus about $11.43 against $10.60-11.85 implied), so it needs a beat. Valmont beat its last two quarters: Q2 $6.14 against $5.80 consensus, revenue $1.12bn against $1.09bn; Q3 2025 $4.98 against $4.62. Q3 consensus of $5.73 is +15% y/y, below Q2's +26% y/y adjusted growth. Q3 2025 itself rose +1.36% on a beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats were paid in Q1 2026 (+11.9%) and Feb 2025 (+17.5%), barely paid in Q3 2025 (+1.4%), and sold in Q2 2026 (-3.9%). Mixed.
findings.why_not_priced: A beat cadence is visible to everyone; the only possible edge is that Q3 growth expectations (+15%) step down from Q2 (+26%) while the utility mix stays strong. Largely priced; sized small.
findings.independence: Q2 numbers: company 8-K ex99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000102729/000110465926085223/vmi-20260721xex99d1.htm . Q3 2025 beat: https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/valmont-reports-q3-adjusted-eps-4-98-consensus-4-62-thefly

findings.finding: USDA's 2026-09-03 farm income forecast raised 2026 net farm income to $158.4bn from $153.4bn in February, with direct government payments up $19.5bn to $47.4bn and corn receipts +11.3%. Production costs are at a record $492.8bn (+4.5%). This marginally firms the NA irrigation outlook after Ag sales fell 15.8% in Q2 (NA -2.3%, International -28.9% on the Middle East conflict, Ag backlog $91.3m from $105.4m). The Ag guide of $0.9-0.95bn was held, and management guided H2 Ag margins to 'low teens'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4 2025 print (02-17), led by an Ag miss, fell 6.6%. Ag was weak but held in Q2 2026, and the stock fell 3.9% on margin tone.
findings.why_not_priced: A macro series, public and wire-carried. It matters only for the 2027 Ag tone on the call, which consensus has not been seen to move. Small.
findings.independence: Farm Bureau, https://www.fb.org/market-intel/usda-revises-farm-income-higher-but-costs-still-bite , reports the same USDA data and stresses cost pressure, so it shares the source. Lindsay's FQ3 (June) had NA irrigation -11%, which predates Valmont's call: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/836157/000119312526138910/lnn-ex99_1.htm

findings.why_not_priced: It is on the wire, so mostly priced. The stock did not bounce after Oct 16 (5-day run-up -5.0% to Oct 19), which suggests the survey was not read as a strong positive. Snippet only; sized small.

baseline_tension: The findings net slightly positive, in line with the upside-paid skew (-4.6) and the de-rated price (-24% off the high). The steel finding cuts the other way, and the Q2 sell-off on a beat-and-raise argues that this holder base sells good quarters when the margin tone is soft. Net, p_up sits near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the beat-cadence finding went from +0.4 to +0.2, because the Q2 beat-and-raise sold off 3.9%.

Rule 5 / core table (macro-to-company transmission): steel went from -1.0 to -0.7, because part of the rise was in the 07-17 futures the guide used and Valmont passes steel through to utility customers with a lag; the USDA Ag finding went from +0.3 to +0.2.
Rule 9 (net of the rest of the company): utility demand went from +0.6 to +0.4, because Valmont says growth is supply-limited, and telecom (down teens) and Ag are guided drags.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): the bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing Benzinga snapshots, so no cap was applied.

Rule 7 (positioning): short interest checked, 2.2% and 2.0 days to cover, not crowded; the negative steel finding is not shrunk for squeeze risk but stays small against the upside-paid skew. p_up went from 53 to 52.
